feedback: The confession follows the exact contradiction available before voting: Sue invents an eyewitness pour at the prepared place when the independent record places pouring in the kitchen. Her taking poison during the preview is a new explicit detail of execution, but it supplies no new decisive deduction; the preview access and real bottle were already established. The threatened ownership advice also gives her motive a prior foundation. Monet and Elon resolve their competing lies plausibly into financial misconduct. Sue's final address to Mona adds a relational cost beyond avoiding professional exposure, although its polished phrasing continues the recurring closing-speech style. The result feels earned and emotionally coherent, with the key proof remaining available to readers before confession.
